stages.label: Seed
stages.biology: A single rose achene rests partly embedded in moist soil.

stages.label: Germination
stages.biology: After its dormancy requirements are met, the radicle and curved shoot emerge.

stages.label: Seedling
stages.biology: Cotyledons open before the first serrated true leaves develop.

stages.label: Vegetative Growth
stages.biology: The perennial plant builds stems, leaves, roots, and stored energy before flowering.

stages.label: Flower Bud
stages.biology: Sepals enclose and protect the developing petals and reproductive structures.

stages.label: Bloom Opening
stages.biology: Petals separate and unfold over several days, depending on cultivar and weather.

stages.label: Full Bloom
stages.biology: The open five-petaled flower exposes its stamens and receptive floral structures.

stages.label: Pollination
stages.biology: Pollen is transferred to receptive stigmas while the bloom is open.

stages.label: Petals Fall
stages.biology: The petals detach while the fertilized floral base begins fruit development.

stages.label: Rose Hip & Seeds
stages.biology: The fleshy hypanthium matures into a rose hip enclosing seed-bearing achenes.

stages.label: Plant Death
stages.biology: Because roses are perennial, whole-plant death is an eventual stage years later rather than an immediate result of producing a rose hip; the stem and leaves wilt and desiccate, the hip shrivels, and the fallen petals rest on the soil.
